title: Zuri's Sparkly Light
markdown:
Zuri loved to build, build, build. Her robot pal Bloop went “Bzzzt! Beep-boop!” when he was happy.

It was time for the Big Lantern Festival. Zuri wanted her lantern SUPER sparkly. In her workshop she gathered crinkly foil, a smooth glass marble, and a shiny mirror. She stuck them on a plain box. It just looked like the room, but box-shaped. No glow. She sighed a tiny sigh and turned the box around, hoping the other side had learned to shine. It had not.

WHOOSH. Bloop zipped in. “Bzzzt! Lantern fun?” Zuri showed him the dull box. “It just shows me what’s already there.” Bloop nudged a lamp. Click. Warm light of its own. He pointed to the bright sun, then the lamp, then the box that only copied.

Zuri’s eyes popped. “The sun makes light! And the lamp makes light too!” She held her mirror to the lamp. The light bounced. The mirror itself did not glow. “It just sends light back.” Bloop beeped. She had used things that only reflect — foil, marble, mirror. She needed things that make light, like the sun and the lamp. A happy wiggle started. What a discovery.

Coach Ellis bounced in. “Ready to shine?” Zuri jumped up. “We need things that make light!” She found tiny LED bulbs, like jewels. Bloop offered special paper that could glow. With Ellis they decorated a new box, poked holes for the little bulbs, wired them so the switches sat in a neat row. Click. Click. Click. The lantern sprang to life with its own soft glow, shining all by itself. “It’s glowing!” Zuri giggled. Bloop did a happy spin that nearly knocked the old dull box off the bench.

Then the lantern parade. Zuri’s lantern bobbed, casting a warm circle. Other lanterns twinkled: bright bulbs, glow-sticks, flickering candles. She watched them all and understood. Some things make light. Other things, like her first mirror, only catch it. The night filled with the ones that made their own.

She did not ask what other secrets waited. She carried the dull box home as a reminder, and let Bloop carry the glowing one, because he had pointed at the lamp first.
